**Step 1 — Scene:** A cooked breakfast: two fried eggs, grilled tomato halves and mushrooms. I’m estimating the main plate only; the toast on the separate plate, yogurt and drink are excluded.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** The main plate appears approximately **23 cm** in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 11.5² ≈ **415 cm²**.

**Steps 3–6 — Items, coverage, volume and weight:**

| Item | Plate coverage | Area | Typical height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Two eggs | 34% | 141 cm² | 0.75 cm | 106 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 106 g |
| Grilled tomato halves | 20% | 83 cm² | 1.7 cm | 141 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 85 g |
| Mushrooms | 6% | 25 cm² | 1.5 cm | 38 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 22 g |
| Visible cooking-fat sheen | Overlaps food | — | Thin film | ~4.4 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 4 g |

Food covers approximately **60% of the plate**. The fat overlaps those footprints rather than adding separate coverage.

**Step 7 — Energy:** Eggs: 106 × 155/100 ≈ 164 kcal; tomatoes: 85 × 20/100 ≈ 17 kcal; mushrooms: 22 × 28/100 ≈ 6 kcal; cooking fat: 4 × 880/100 ≈ 35 kcal. Fat is counted separately to avoid double-counting it in the eggs.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **217 g and 222 kcal** is plausible for two eggs, two tomato halves, a few mushrooms and a light coating of cooking fat.
